b run1.one_line_characterisation: Five stakeholders with orthogonal constraints negotiated a testing sequence rather than resolving the underlying decision, with Marcus shifting from demanding measurement-first to accepting design-first only after Dana reframed the logical impossibility of his request.

b run2.one_line_characterisation: Five stakeholders with orthogonal constraints (infrastructure, cost, hallucination risk, auditability, sales velocity) negotiated toward a testable architecture (SQLite-embedded retrieval with token measurement) without anyone abandoning their core requirement.

b run3.one_line_characterisation: Five stakeholders each articulated a non-negotiable prerequisite gate (install speed, token cost, retrieval quality, auditability, customer-facing capability) and held them in parallel without resolving which gate must be satisfied first.

d run1.one_line_characterisation: Five stakeholders built consensus on technical constraints (embedding, versioning, auditability) while diverging sharply on whether those constraints solve the actual customer problem, with Simone and Priya naming different risks the others were optimizing away.

d run2.one_line_characterisation: The group converged on a measurement protocol after Simone and Dana repeatedly misaligned on whether the test should measure cost or justify viability, with Priya introducing a reasoning-quality concern that remained orthogonal to the final decision gate.

d run3.one_line_characterisation: Five stakeholders with initially competing constraints (sales velocity, cost transparency, system maintainability, deployment simplicity, and feature reliability) negotiated toward a shared sequential decision process—spike first, measure second, ship only if all constraints hold—without anyone abandoning their core requirement.
